clips.title: Why Handcrafted AI Breaks at Scale
clips.summary: Early neural networks treated intelligence like a handcrafted machine. The break came when that approach stopped scaling.

clips.title: ResNet Fixed the Depth Problem
clips.summary: ResNet worked because it stopped forcing every layer to rewrite the whole signal and let layers learn residual corrections instead.

clips.title: The Transformer Won as a Portable Block
clips.summary: Transformers mattered not just because of attention, but because the whole block became portable across domains once wrapped in a stable residual scaffold.

clips.title: Transformer Portability Depends on Scale
clips.summary: Vision Transformers did not kill inductive bias. They only beat ResNets once scale supplied enough data to learn structure from scratch.

clips.title: The Compute Recipe Became the Design
clips.summary: Once transformer behavior became predictable under scaling laws, architecture design moved upward into budgets, data allocation, and training recipes.

clips.title: MoE Is Controlled Heterogeneity
clips.summary: Mixture-of-experts looks like a return to messy heterogeneity, but the specialization is now governed by routing inside a stable scaffold.
